question.text: Research analysts need to study savings and investment patterns in an economy primarily because:

answer.text: It helps predict the exact stock prices of banking companies
Higher savings converted to investments indicate potential growth in the economy and markets
SEBI requires all research reports to include a savings analysis section
Savings data is the only indicator of a country's economic health

explanation.text: The Logic: Higher levels of savings and a higher conversion of those savings into investments are considered good for an economy, because savings get channelized into productive investments. The Trap: Option A overstates the predictive power. Option C is not a regulatory requirement. Option D is incorrect — savings is one of several indicators of economic health, not the only one. Note: The workbook's point is the macro link between savings, investment, and economic growth — not a specific claim about company-level stock prices.
